title: Quality: which product, which heading, which role
blurb: Place quality information under the right heading of the quality management approach, a product description or the quality register, and match quality actions to roles.
question: Fernhollow Foods' co-manufacturer will make two recipes under its own certified quality management system. Under which heading of the quality management approach should this be recorded?

teach.h: Four quality products, four different jobs
teach.body: Formally, the quality practice documents the user's requirements of the project's products and establishes the means by which they will be met. Its products are the quality management approach (how quality will be achieved across the project), product descriptions (what each product must be), the quality register (what quality checks were planned and done) and the product register (every product of a plan and its status). In plain English: the rulebook, the spec sheet, the test log and the stock list.

head: Heading
Holds
Fernhollow example
teach.caption: Full heading: supporting tools and techniques. A requirement that every supplier holds a quality policy is a quality standard and belongs in the quality management approach.

teach.h: A product description for one recipe
head: Heading
Lentil dahl example
teach.caption: Quality specifications are the functional and non-functional requirements with their measures. The responsibilities show who produces, reviews and approves the product, including sustainability responsibilities.

head: Heading
Entry
teach.caption: The quality register summarizes all quality activities planned or performed. A failed check may be repeated if a pass is expected after rework.

teach.body: The board approves the project product description and the quality management approach. The PM prepares product descriptions for key products and the quality management approach, and in 'receive completed work package' makes sure each product has its required approval. The team manager updates the quality register and tells the PM when quality activities are complete. The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of supplier products. Quality assurance is done independently of the project management team.

teach.text: Project assurance is not quality assurance. Project assurance is the board's responsibility, independent of the PM but part of the project. Quality assurance is a business or programme function outside the project management team that checks the project's quality controls are appropriate.

teach.body: Nadia Osei, the project manager, writes the quality management approach in initiation. Greendale's certified system goes under references; who accepts each recipe under responsibilities; consumer panels and shelf-life tests under tools and techniques; the required format for test records under standards. Each recipe's eight-day shelf life is a quality specification in its product description. Megan Cho's chefs log every tasting in the quality register, and Nadia uses the product register to see which recipes are approved.

items: Ask the scope: does it apply to all quality work (approach) or one product (product description)?
Approach: an outside quality system is references; who plans, checks and accepts is responsibilities.
Approach: test or trial methods are tools and techniques; rules and record formats are standards.
Register: the check used is the method; when is dates; who is responsibilities; pass or fail is result.
Quality management approach: references, responsibilities, supporting tools and techniques, standards (8.5).
Product description: purpose, composition, derivation, format, quality specifications, method, responsibilities.
Quality register: quality method, dates, responsibilities, result (8.5).
Product register: all products of a plan and their status.
Quality assurance is independent of the project management team; project assurance is the board's.

summary: You can now place quality facts under the right heading of the quality management approach, a product description or the quality register. You can also match quality actions to the board, project manager, team manager and quality assurance.

A.q: Fernhollow Foods is writing the quality management approach for its Fernhollow Kitchen range during initiation. It states that the quality register and all test records must follow a set layout, with batch codes and test conditions recorded for every check. Under which heading should this be recorded?
A.why: The standards heading covers any standards that apply to quality management, including the composition and format of the quality register and other quality records (8.5).

whyNot.0: References point to associated documents such as the business's or a supplier's quality management system.
whyNot.2: Responsibilities define who does quality planning, control and acceptance.
whyNot.3: Supporting tools and techniques cover methods such as testing, inspection and trials.

A.q: Fernhollow Kitchen's product description for its lentil dahl states that the meal must keep for at least eight days chilled and contain no more than a set level of salt per portion. Under which heading of the product description should this be recorded?
A.why: Quality specifications are the functional and non-functional requirements for the product with their measures (8.5).

whyNot.0: Quality method is how the product will be checked, such as a shelf-life test, not the requirement itself.
whyNot.1: Quality tolerance is the permitted deviation from the specification before escalation, not the requirement itself.
whyNot.2: Quality responsibilities name the producer, reviewers and approvers, not what the product must achieve.

A.q: Fernhollow Kitchen's quality register has an entry for the shelf-life test of the lentil dahl. The entry must show that Luke Barraclough, the technical and quality manager, reviewed the results and that Megan Cho, head of new product development, approved the recipe. Under which quality register heading does this go?
A.why: The responsibilities heading records the individuals or functions involved and their roles, such as reviewer and approver (8.5).

whyNot.1: Result records whether the product passed or failed and the response to a failure.
whyNot.2: Quality method records the method used, here the shelf-life test.
whyNot.3: Dates record planned and actual dates of the activity.

B.q: Fernhollow Foods' co-manufacturer, Greendale Ready Meals, will make two of the six recipes. Its own certified quality management system will govern how those recipes are made. Under which heading of Fernhollow Kitchen's quality management approach should this be recorded?
B.why: References list associated documents or products, such as the business's or a supplier's quality management systems (8.5).

whyNot.0: Standards cover rules for quality management such as register format, not pointers to a supplier's quality system.
whyNot.1: Responsibilities define who does quality planning, control and acceptance.
whyNot.3: Supporting tools and techniques describe methods such as testing and inspection.

B.q: Fernhollow Kitchen's development stage plan has 23 products. Nadia Osei, the project manager, needs to see at a glance which recipes, packs and line components are in development, approved or handed over. Which product should she use?
B.why: The product register lists all products required of a plan and their status (8.5).

whyNot.1: The quality register records quality activities and their results, not every product's status.
whyNot.2: The issue register records formal issues.
whyNot.3: The daily log holds informal issues, actions and notes.

B.q: Megan Cho's team has finished the recipe work package for Fernhollow Kitchen. Before treating the work package as complete, someone must make sure each recipe has the approval required by the responsibilities in its product description. Which role should do this?
B.why: In 'receive completed work package' the project manager makes sure each product has gained its requisite approval as defined by the quality and sustainability responsibilities in its product description (16.4.3).

whyNot.0: The team manager notifies completion; the PM receives the work package and checks the approvals.
whyNot.1: Project assurance can review that quality controls are working, but receiving the work package is the PM's activity.
whyNot.2: The senior user may be an approver of some products, but confirming every approval on receipt is the PM's job.

C.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. Nadia Osei records in the quality management approach that every supplier, including the co-manufacturer and the packaging supplier, must hold a certified food safety and quality policy. Is this an appropriate application of the 'quality' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because the quality register summarizes all quality activities
Yes, because the approach describes the quality standards to be followed
No, because supplier requirements belong in each work package description
No, because the business layer's quality system already covers suppliers
C.why: The quality management approach describes the quality standards and procedures to be followed, so a standard required of all suppliers belongs in it (8.3.1.1, 8.5).

whyNot.0: It is true that the register summarizes quality activities, but that does not explain recording a supplier standard in the approach.
whyNot.2: Work package descriptions carry instructions for specific work; a standard for all suppliers is set once in the approach.
whyNot.3: The business's quality system may be a reference, but the project still states the standards it requires.

C.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Megan Cho, team manager for the recipe work package, records each consumer panel tasting result in the quality register and tells Nadia Osei, the project manager, when each round of tastings is complete. Is this an appropriate application of the 'quality' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because team managers notify completed quality activities
Yes, because the senior user provides the quality expectations
No, because project support maintains the registers for the PM
No, because quality results go in the checkpoint report instead
C.why: In 'execute a work package' the team manager notifies the PM of completed quality activities and updates the quality register (17.4.2).

whyNot.1: It is true that the senior user provides quality expectations, but that does not explain the team manager's actions.
whyNot.2: Project support often maintains registers, but the team manager also updates the quality register when executing a work package.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports summarize status, but quality results are recorded in the quality register.

C.q: Fernhollow Kitchen must pass a supermarket audit. Luke Barraclough, the technical and quality manager, runs a function that is independent of production and sits outside the project management team. The managing director asks him to check whether the project's planned quality controls are appropriate to meet the audit. Is this an appropriate application of the 'quality' practice, and why?
options: Yes, because project assurance is independent of the project manager
Yes, because quality assurance is done independently of the PMT
No, because quality assurance is a responsibility of the project board
No, because the PM makes sure team managers apply quality controls
C.why: Quality assurance is a planned, systematic activity performed independently of the project management team, for example by a business quality function, checking that the project's quality controls are appropriate (8.2.3).

whyNot.0: It is true project assurance is independent of the PM, but Luke sits outside the PMT and is doing quality assurance.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is the board's responsibility; quality assurance is a business or programme function.
whyNot.3: The PM does see that controls are applied, but that does not stop an independent function checking them.

reteach.title: Rulebook, spec sheet, test log, stock list
reteach.question: If you ran a test kitchen, where would you write the house rules, each dish's spec, each tasting and the list of dishes?

blocks.h: Match the fact to the document's job
blocks.body: House rules for every dish (which outside standards apply, who tastes and approves, how tests are run, how records look) go in the quality management approach. What one dish must achieve goes in its product description. Each tasting or test, with date, who and result, goes in the quality register. The list of every dish and where it stands goes in the product register.

steps.label: Approach
steps.sub: Shelf-life testing required for all recipes

blocks.text: A supplier's own quality management system is a reference; the format required for quality records is a standard. Read whether the fact points OUT to another system or sets a RULE for the project.

explain.body: It describes the quality techniques and standards to be applied and the roles and responsibilities for meeting quality specifications and acceptance criteria. Headings: references, responsibilities, supporting tools and techniques, standards. It is created in initiation and approved by the board.

test.q: Fernhollow Kitchen's quality management approach must state that the technical team will review every recipe before it is approved, and that the sales and marketing director is the acceptance authority for the finished range. Under which heading does this belong?
test.why: Responsibilities define who carries out quality planning and control, including project assurance and acceptance authorities (8.5).

whyNot.0: Supporting tools and techniques describe methods such as testing and trials.
whyNot.1: References point to other quality systems or documents.
whyNot.2: Standards are rules such as record formats.

explain.body: It describes one product's purpose, composition, derivation, format and quality specifications, with the quality method, tolerance, skills and the producer, reviewer and approver responsibilities. The PM prepares product descriptions for key products.

test.q: Fernhollow's product description for the lentil dahl says the recipe comes from the version the consumer panel preferred in tasting round four. Under which heading does this belong?
test.why: Derivation records where the product comes from, such as its source (8.5).

whyNot.2: Purpose explains why the product is needed.
whyNot.3: Quality method is how the product will be checked.

explain.body: The quality register summarizes all quality activities planned or performed: quality method, dates, responsibilities and result. The product register lists all products of a plan and their status. Both sit in the project log and are checked and closed in closing a project.

test.q: Fernhollow Kitchen's shelf-life test of the mushroom stroganoff failed at day seven, and a retest has been booked after a recipe change. Under which quality register heading is the failure and the retest recorded?
test.why: Result records whether the product passed or failed and the response in the event of a failure (8.5).

whyNot.0: Dates hold planned and actual dates.
whyNot.1: Quality method names the check used.

explain.body: Board: approves the PPD and the quality management approach. PM: prepares product descriptions and the approach; checks approvals when receiving work packages. Team manager: updates the quality register and notifies completed quality activities. Senior supplier: accountable for supplier product quality. Quality assurance: independent of the PMT.

test.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in initiation. Which role should approve the quality management approach?
test.why: In directing a project the board approves the project product description and the quality management approach (tab 14.3).

whyNot.0: Team managers apply the approach in their work packages.
whyNot.3: Quality assurance sits outside the project management team and does not approve project products.
